item.title: Xi replies to U.S. university students
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
Xi replies to U.S. university students BEIJING -- Chinese President Xi Jinping recently replied to students from 10 U.S. universities who wrote to him after attending youth exchanges in China. Xi noted that he was delighted to learn that the students enjoyed a pleasant and memorable journey in China. Xi said he was pleased to hear that the students expressed in the letter their appreciation for Chinese civilization, their hope for friendly cooperation between China and the United States, and their willingness to act as envoys of friendship bridging the Pacific Ocean. Young people from China and the United States, Xi said, share the same planet Earth and jointly shoulder the mission of the times. He expressed hope that the students would join the vast number of young people in both countries in striving to carry forward, uphold, and advance China-U.S. friendly cooperation, and work together to foster mutual understanding and affinity between the two peoples and to ensure the steady and long-term development of bilateral relations, so as to contribute the vitality of youth to building a better world. Recently, nearly 100 students from Harvard University and nine other U.S. universities wrote to Xi, sharing their experiences and what they had gained from the Future Makers 2026 China-U.S. Youth Tour for a Shared Asia-Pacific Future and other exchange events in China, and expressing their willingness to contribute to promoting China-U.S. friendship.

item.title: Xi to pay state visit to U.S. from Sept. 23 to 25
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
Xi to pay state visit to U.S. from Sept. 23 to 25 BEIJING -- Chinese President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from Sept. 23 to 25 at the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Monday. During the visit, Xi and Trump will have an in-depth exchange of views on major issues concerning China-U.S. relations and world peace and development, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a regular news briefing. Head-of-state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance for China-U.S. relations, and the exchange of visits between the two heads of state within six months marks a historic milestone, Guo said. China is ready to work with the U.S. side to enrich the connotation of the constructive relationship of strategic stability, enhance dialogue and cooperation, properly manage differences, and continuously contribute to the well-being of both peoples and global peace, stability and prosperity, he added.

item.title: CPC leadership meeting studies major issues on Party self-governance, sets dates for Party plenum
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
CPC leadership meeting studies major issues on Party self-governance, sets dates for Party plenum BEIJING -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on Monday chaired a meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, which studied major issues on strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance and set the dates for an upcoming Party plenum in October. The meeting decided that the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC will be held from Oct. 26 to 29 in Beijing. The meeting also decided to submit a document on the CPC Central Committee's decision regarding strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance to the plenum for deliberation. An earlier draft of the decision was circulated among Party members and non-Party figures for comment, drawing broad support from those consulted. The meeting noted that the document provides an objective assessment of the achievements and experience in advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance in the new era, offers an in-depth analysis of the situation and tasks facing Party building in the present and coming period, and sets out strategic plans for continuing to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance. The meeting stressed that, to strengthen full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance, it is imperative to uphold the Party's overall leadership and the centralized, unified leadership of the CPC Central Committee, maintain a strict approach without wavering, and improve the systems for exercising full and rigorous self-governance. Efforts must be made to ensure that the Party remains a vibrant Marxist governing party that stays at the forefront of the times, enjoys the wholehearted support of the people, withstands all tests, and serves as the strong leadership core in building socialism with Chinese characteristics, said the meeting. The meeting called for fully recognizing the significance and urgency of unswervingly advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance, adopting higher standards and taking more concrete measures to address the prominent issues facing Party building. Other matters were also discussed at the meeting.

item.title: Speech at the Ceremony Marking the 105th Anniversary of the Founding of the Communist Party of China
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-18
Speech at the Ceremony Marking the 105th Anniversary of the Founding of the Communist Party of China XI JINPING Comrades and friends, Today, we gather to celebrate the 105th anniversary of the founding of the Communist Party of China. We meet to reflect on the glorious journey our Party has traveled, to look ahead to the bright prospects for the cause of our Party and our people, and to rally all Party members and the Chinese people to march with confidence and courage toward the goal of building a great modern socialist country and realizing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. First, on behalf of our Party’s Central Committee, I would like to extend greetings to all members of our Party on this occasion. I also wish to warmly congratulate the recipients of the July 1 Medal, as well as the outstanding Party members, exemplary Party affairs workers, and advanced primary-level Party organizations from across the country being honored here today. Comrades and friends, One hundred and five years ago, out of the great awakening of the Chinese people and the Chinese nation and the close integration of Marxism-Leninism with the Chinese workers’ movement, the Communist Party of China was born. From that moment on, the Chinese people and the Chinese nation had in the Party a truly dependable anchor. The long-enfeebled and impoverished China, embattled by internal turmoil and foreign aggression, thus embarked on a historic and earthshaking transformation. General Secretary Xi Jinping addresses a gathering marking the 105th founding anniversary of the CPC, held at the Great Hall of the People, Beijing, July 1, 2026. PHOTO BY XINHUA REPORTER YAO DAWEI Over the past 105 years, our Party has remained true to its original aspiration and founding mission: to seek happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation. With a deep insight into the prevailing trends of global development and an accurate grasp of the principal challenges facing Chinese society in each historical period, it has united and led the Chinese people in pursuing tireless endeavor. Together, we have achieved great accomplishments in the new-democratic revolution; in socialist revolution and construction; in reform, opening up, and socialist modernization; and in socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era—writing the most magnificent chapter in the millennia-long history of the Chinese nation. General Secretary Xi Jinping awards the July 1 Medal to the recipients at a gathering marking the 105th founding anniversary of the CPC, held at the Great Hall of the People, Beijing, July 1, 2026. PHOTO BY XINHUA REPORTER SHEN HONG Through 105 years of tireless endeavor, we have fundamentally reshaped the future and destiny of the Chinese people. Our Party led the people through a great and surging struggle, toppling the three mountains of imperialism, feudalism, and bureaucrat-capitalism and founding the People’s Republic of China where the people become the masters of the country, thus finally bringing an end to the semi-colonial, semi-feudal history of old China. We achieved a historic transformation in living standards, rising from bare subsistence to moderate prosperity in general, and then to moderate prosperity in all respects. Today, the Chinese people hold their future firmly in their own hands, and with confidence, self-reliance, and strength, they are striding toward an even brighter tomorrow. Through 105 years of tireless endeavor, we have carved out the right path toward national rejuvenation. Throughout the periods of revolution, construction, reform, and the new era, our Party has led the people through untold hardships, charting and following the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics. In just a few decades, we have completed an industrialization process that took developed countries several centuries, and in doing so, we have achieved the two miracles of rapid economic growth and enduring social stability. Today, the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is advancing with irresistible momentum, unfolding prospects brighter than ever before. Through 105 years of tireless endeavor, we have demonstrated the immense vitality of Marxism. Our Party has consistently integrated the basic tenets of Marxism with China’s specific realities and the best elements of its traditional culture, continuously adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of the times. This has given rise to Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Theory of Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development, and the Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, enriching and developing Marxism in the process. Today, all the vigor and vitality of Chinese socialism stand as ample proof of Marxism’s scientific nature and objective truth, its people-centered and practical orientation, and its openness and capacity to advance with the times. Through 105 years of tireless endeavor, we have profoundly influenced the course of world history. Always standing on the right side of history and on the side of human progress, our Party has, through its continuing efforts, profoundly reshaped the trajectory and landscape of global development. Today, by leading the people in advancing Chinese modernization, we have created a new form of human civilization and broadened the pathways by which developing countries can achieve modernization. By promoting the building of a community with a shared future for humanity, we are contributing Chinese wisdom, Chinese solutions, and Chinese strength to resolving the major challenges facing humankind. Under the Party’s leadership, socialist China is recognized the world over as a builder of world peace, a contributor to global development, and a defender of the international order. Through 105 years of tireless endeavor, we have forged a strong Communist Party of China. Ever mindful of its nature and purpose as a Marxist party and the goals toward which it strives, our Party has carried forward its great founding spirit. Through every hardship, our will has been tempered; through every trial, we have emerged only stronger. Today, our Party is the world’s largest governing party, with significant influence on the global stage. Having the wholehearted endorsement and support of our people, it serves as the strong leadership core of the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Without question, it has proved itself fully worthy of being called a great, glorious, and correct party. Comrades and friends, We owe all that we have achieved over the past 105 years to the tireless endeavor of the Chinese people, united and led by generation after generation of Chinese Communists. These Chinese Communists, with Comrades Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, and Hu Jintao as their chief representatives, have made tremendous and historic contributions to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. To them, we pay the highest tribute. Let us take this moment to honor the memory of Comrades Mao Zedong, Zhou Enlai, Liu Shaoqi, Zhu De, Deng Xiaoping, Chen Yun, and other revolutionaries of the older generation, and the memory of Comrade Jiang Zemin. We honor as well the revolutionary martyrs and noble-minded patriots who gave their lives, or devoted their all, to national independence, the liberation of the people, the prosperity of the nation, and the happiness of the people. The monumental contributions they made to our country and our nation are engraved forever in the annals of history, and their lofty spirit will endure in the hearts of millions upon millions of our people. The people are the creators of history; they are the true heroes. Here, on behalf of the Central Committee, I would like to pay our highest respects to people working diligently on every front across the nation, and to public figures from all sectors of society. I would like to extend our sincere greetings to our fellow countrymen and women in the Hong Kong and Macao special administrative regions, in Taiwan, and residing overseas. And I would like to express our heartfelt gratitude to people and friends around the world who have shown friendship to the Chinese people and understanding and support for China’s endeavors in revolution, construction, and reform. Comrades and friends, Our Party has been able to achieve one glory after another over its 105-year journey and earn the recognition of history and the people, fundamentally because it possesses the following fine qualities unmatched by any other political party or force. • A dedication to the pursuit of truth enables our Party to always advance in the right direction. Regarding Marxism as a powerful intellectual instrument for transforming both our subjective and objective worlds, our Party has remained committed to freeing the mind, seeking truth from facts, advancing with the times, and taking a realistic and pragmatic approach. It has endeavored to reveal and apply the truth within the evolving contradictions of society, to test and develop that truth through practice, and to use new theories to guide new practice. This ensures that the cause of the Party and the people always advances in the right direction. • Deep roots among the people enable our Party to always stand on solid ground. Based on the firm belief that this country is the people and the people are the country, our Party has committed itself to serving the public good and governing for the people. It has consciously fulfilled its fundamental purpose of wholeheartedly serving the people, standing firmly with the people, sharing their aspirations, and working alongside them. All this has created a strong and unshakable foundation for our Party. • A determination to shoulder its historic mission enables our Party to always maintain the strategic initiative. Guided by the lofty ideal of communism and a firm commitment to achieving lasting greatness for the Chinese nation, our Party has carried upon its shoulders the heavy responsibilities entrusted to it by history and the people. Aligning long-term goals with objectives of each stage, it has defined its central tasks in response to changes in the principal challenge facing Chinese society, and it has formulated and implemented the correct line, principles, and policies to maintain leadership and initiative in advancing our development. • A readiness to adapt to the trends of development enables our Party to always remain at the forefront of the times. With a keen sense of history and a broad global vision, our Party has maintained a clear grasp of China’s actual conditions and the defining themes of the times, proactively identifying, responding to, and steering changes. Forging ahead with determination and a pioneering spirit, it has ensured that all its undertakings advance with the times, conform to the objective laws of development, and are innovative in nature. In this way, it has steered the country and the nation forward in step with the logic of history and the trends of development, fully proving itself a pioneer of the times and the backbone of the nation. • The courage and competence to carry on its fight enable our Party to always maintain firm confidence in victory. Bearing in mind the interests of the people, the country, and the nation as well as its ideals and convictions, our Party has fought bravely and forged ahead against all odds without fear of sacrifice. No matter how formidable the adversary, how treacherous the path, or how severe the challenge, it has remained undaunted and unyielding. With an iron will that no storm or difficulty can shake, it has inspired the people of the entire country to advance from one victory to the next. • A commitment to self-strengthening enables our Party to always retain its vitality. Keenly aware that it takes a good blacksmith to forge good steel, our Party is committed to examining itself through the lens of the changing times, keeping itself alert through a strong awareness of potential dangers, and improving itself in a spirit of self-reform. We attach great importance to self-improvement and are determined to remove any elements that would harm the Party’s advanced nature and integrity and any viruses that would erode the Party’s health. It is through this revolutionary tempering that our Party has grown ever stronger. These fine qualities hold the key to the success of the Communist Party of China. We must continue to develop and carry forward these qualities in line with new realities to ensure that the Party never changes its nature, its convictions, or its character and always maintains strong creativity, cohesion, and capability. Comrades and friends, Great accomplishments are built through aspiration and diligence. To fulfill the Party’s mission and tasks on the new journey in the new era, all Chinese Communists must stand firm in confidence and carry on our endeavor, continuously delivering new feats worthy of the times and the people. • To remain confident and carry on our endeavor, we must uphold the Party’s basic theory, basic line, and basic policy. These are major achievements secured through painstaking exploration by the Party and the people, and they serve as the fundamental guide for advancing the development of the Party and the country. On the journey ahead, the whole Party must maintain the resolve to keep to our path and uphold our convictions. We must uphold the Party’s overall leadership and the centralized, unified leadership of the Central Committee, thoroughly implement the Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and remain confident in the path, theory, system, and culture of Chinese socialism. We must build on past achievements to advance our cause, and break new ground while upholding fundamental principles. With all this, our view will never be obscured by passing clouds, and we will brave the wind and waves without ever losing our bearings. General Secretary Xi Jinping and other leaders of the CPC and the state present awards to representatives of outstanding Party members, Party workers, and primary-level Party organizations from across the country at a gathering marking the 105th founding anniversary of the CPC, held at the Great Hall of the People, Beijing, July 1, 2026. PHOTO BY XINHUA REPORTER HUANG JINGWEN • To remain confident and carry on our endeavor, we must rely closely on the people to make further achievements. Upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics is a shared undertaking of the entire Party and the people across the country. On the journey ahead, the whole Party must work with renewed drive and resolve to rally the Chinese people and lead them in breaking new ground. We must ensure coordinated implementation of the Five-Sphere Integrated Plan and the Four-Pronged Comprehensive Strategy, fully and faithfully apply the new development philosophy, and move faster to create a new pattern of development through solid progress in pursuing high-quality development. Acting on the people-centered development philosophy, we must promote whole-process people’s democracy and consolidate and strengthen the great unity of all ethnic groups, of all Chinese people, and of all sons and daughters of the Chinese nation. By unleashing the motivation, initiative, and creativity of more than one billion Chinese people, we will create a mighty force for advancing Chinese modernization. • To remain confident and carry on our endeavor, we must proactively address risks and challenges on the road ahead. China remains in a stage of development where strategic opportunities exist alongside risks and challenges, and uncertainties and unforeseen factors are on the rise. We must be prepared at all times to brave high winds, choppy waters, and even dangerous storms. On the journey ahead, the whole Party must heighten our awareness of potential dangers, keep in mind worst-case scenarios, and strengthen our readiness and competence to carry on our fight. We must better balance domestic and international imperatives, ensure both development and security, and build up our ability to rationally anticipate changes, promptly identify risks, and effectively address challenges. Through these efforts, we will ensure that the giant ship of national rejuvenation can navigate turbulent waters and continue sailing steadily forward. • To remain confident and carry on our endeavor, we must continue to promote the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. With changes unseen in a century unfolding at an ever faster pace, the world has entered a new period of turbulence and transformation. Humanity once again stands at a crossroads, facing a choice about which way to turn. On the journey ahead, we will follow the will of the people and the trend of the times. We will uphold peace, development, cooperation, and mutual benefit, champion the common values of all humanity, and work to foster a new type of international relations. We will act on the Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative, the Global Civilizations Initiative, and the Global Governance Initiative to inject greater positive energy into world peace and development. • To remain confident and carry on our endeavor, we must make unremitting efforts to promote full and rigorous Party self-governance, which remains an ongoing process. On the journey ahead, we must fully implement the thinking on Party development for the new era as well as the overall requirements for strengthening the Party in this era. We will focus on enhancing the Party’s capacity for long-term governance, preserving its advanced nature and integrity, and maintaining its close bond with the people. To this end, we will improve the system for exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, strengthen the Party in all respects with reinforcing its political foundation as the overarching guide, and keep waging the tough, protracted, and all-out battle against corruption. We will further strengthen our Party’s capacity for political leadership, theoretical guidance, organizing the people, and inspiring society, so as to ensure that the Party always remains the strong leadership core in the historic endeavor to uphold and develop socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. Comrades and friends, A strong country must have a strong military, as only then can it guarantee the security of the nation. On the journey ahead, we must fully implement the Party’s thinking on strengthening the military in the new era and our military strategy for this era. We must uphold the Party’s absolute leadership over the people’s armed forces and firmly follow the Chinese path of military development. We will take comprehensive measures to enhance the political loyalty of the armed forces, to strengthen them through reform, scientific and technological advances, and the training of competent personnel, and to run them in accordance with the law. We will promote high-quality modernization of national defense and the armed forces, meet the centenary goals of the People’s Liberation Army as planned, and move faster to build our people’s armed forces into a world-class military, so that they can resolutely defend our national sovereignty, security, and development interests and make greater contributions to world peace and development. Lasting prosperity and stability in Hong Kong and Macao are integral to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. On the journey ahead, we will fully, faithfully, and resolutely implement the One Country, Two Systems policy, under which the people of Hong Kong administer Hong Kong and the people of Macao administer Macao, both with a high degree of autonomy. We will see that Hong Kong and Macao are administered by patriots, ensure that both regions are more effectively governed in accordance with the law, and promote their economic and social development. We will support Hong Kong and Macao in better integrating into and contributing to our country’s overall development. Resolving the Taiwan question and achieving China’s complete reunification is, for our Party, a historic mission and an unshakable commitment. It is also a shared aspiration of all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation. We will fully implement the Party’s overall policy for the new era on resolving the Taiwan question, and uphold the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus. Standing together closely with our Taiwan compatriots, we will promote exchanges, cooperation, and integrated development across the Taiwan Strait. We will resolutely fight against separatist forces aimed at “Taiwan independence” and oppose external interference. With firm resolve, we will continue advancing the great endeavor of national reunification. Comrades and friends, China’s young people are a vital force in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. All of us in the Party must give priority to young people, care for them, and support them, creating the conditions they need to grow and succeed. Young people of the new era: You should firmly follow the Party and its guidance, set lofty ideals for yourselves, shoulder the responsibilities of our times, and weave your personal aspirations into the endeavor of the Party and the country. Do your utmost to seize the day and live up to the promise of youth. On the journey ahead, it falls on you to run this leg of the historic relay, drawing on your youthful vigor and letting your ideals shine bright! Comrades and friends, We take great pride in the glorious history our Party has written over the past 105 years, but we shall never grow complacent or rest on past laurels. By the middle of this century, we are to realize the Second Centenary Goal of building China into a great modern socialist country. Time waits for no one; history waits for no one. It is imperative that all of us in the Party never forget our original aspiration and founding mission, that we always remain modest, prudent, and hard-working, and that we have the courage and ability to carry on our fight. Let us rely on and unite the Chinese people of all ethnic groups and lead them forward on the new journey and achieve great accomplishments in the new era, striving to create new historic glories for our nation! (Originally appeared in Qiushi Journal, Chinese edition, No. 14, 2026)

item.title: Xi stresses sustained efforts to expand, strengthen advanced manufacturing
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
Xi stresses sustained efforts to expand, strengthen advanced manufacturing BEIJING -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged sustained efforts to expand and strengthen advanced manufacturing to provide strong support for advancing Chinese modernization. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction, which was conveyed at a national conference on advanced manufacturing held in Beijing on Wednesday and Thursday. Efforts should be made to ensure both high-quality development and greater security, pursue smart, green and integrated development, and make the country's industrial chains more self-supporting and risk-resilient, Xi stressed. He emphasized the need to accelerate the development of a modernized industrial system with advanced manufacturing as the backbone, and reinforce the foundations of the real economy. Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a speech at the conference. Xi's important instructions provide essential guidance for developing advanced manufacturing, Li said, noting that China must treat developing advanced manufacturing as a major strategic task, and press steadily to boost its strength in manufacturing. Li stressed that next-generation intelligent manufacturing should serve as the primary direction, with greater emphasis on digital and intelligent empowerment, high-end manufacturing and self-reliance, green and low-carbon development, and cross-sector integration. Efforts should be made to continuously strengthen the innovation capacity, competitiveness and overall strength of advanced manufacturing, Li said. Li called for deepening the "AI plus manufacturing" initiative, stepping up guidance and support for enterprises' digital and intelligent transformation, and consolidating the foundation of intelligent software and hardware. China should also advance the deep integration of advanced manufacturing and modern services, foster service-oriented manufacturing, and cultivate advanced manufacturing clusters according to local conditions. In his concluding speech, Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing, also a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, said China should further implement the initiative for high-quality development of key industrial chains, accelerate the building of a high-quality standards system, continue to address disorderly and irrational competition, and create a sound ecosystem for advanced manufacturing.

item.title: Full text of Chinese President Xi Jinping's speech at Session I of the 18th BRICS Summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
Full text of Chinese President Xi Jinping's speech at Session I of the 18th BRICS Summit Chinese President Xi Jinping addresses the Session I of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, Sept. 12, 2026. [Xinhua/Yan Yan] NEW DELHI -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Saturday delivered a speech at the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India. The following is the full text of the speech: Jointly Shouldering the Responsibility of the Times and Striving to Be a Pioneering Force Statement by H.E. Xi Jinping President of the People's Republic of China At Session I of the 18th BRICS Summit New Delhi, September 12, 2026 Your Excellency Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Colleagues, It gives me great pleasure to join you in New Delhi. I thank Prime Minister Modi and the Indian government for the thoughtful arrangements. This year marks the 20th anniversary of BRICS cooperation. Over the past two decades, BRICS has been growing with strong vigor and vitality, and become the most influential cooperation platform in today's world for emerging markets and developing countries. These are 20 years of self-reliance and self-strengthening. Standing at the forefront of the Global South, we BRICS countries have upheld independence, actively explored development paths suited to our respective national conditions, and set a fine example of emerging markets and developing countries seeking strength through unity. These are 20 years of standing together through wind and rain. BRICS countries have been forging ahead with an undaunted spirit. Hand in hand we tackled the global financial crisis, COVID pandemic, climate change and other challenges, and we resolutely defended the common interests of the Global South, providing the world with stability and positive energy. These are 20 years of fruitful outcomes. BRICS has realized a historic expansion, and now has a comprehensive, multifaceted cooperation structure with ever deepening cooperation in trade, investment, finance and technology, among others. It has entered a new stage of high-quality development of greater BRICS cooperation. Today, changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world. The Global South is gaining strength, and the trend toward a multipolar world is unstoppable. At the same time, unilateralism and power politics are surging against the tide, lashing at multilateralism and the international order. The deficits in peace, development, security and governance keep growing. For the exact purpose of addressing these deficits and building a better world, I have put forward the Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative, the Global Civilization Initiative and the Global Governance Initiative. BRICS must stand firmly on the right side of history, strive to be a pioneer of our times, steer the international order in a direction that is more just and equitable, and work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity. First, BRICS should be a pioneer in advancing innovation-driven development. The new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation represented by AI is bringing breakthroughs at a faster pace, shaping the global development landscape. We BRICS countries must keep the initiative firmly in our hands, strengthen cooperation in the field of AI, encourage open source, openness, collaboration and sharing, and break new grounds and scale new heights in our practical cooperation. Not long ago, China, together with various parties, initiated the World AI Cooperation Organization, and has developed international AI application cooperation centers with BRICS and others, which provide important platforms for closer AI cooperation for the world, particularly Global South countries. We welcome the active participation of BRICS countries. Here, I propose the BRICS initiative of AI-empowered new industrialization. China hopes to work with all parties for more outcomes in R&D and application and deeper cooperation in industrial and supply chains. Facts will prove that decoupling and cutting off supply chains will not hold back our development process, and espousing "small yard, high fences" will only box oneself in and divide the world. Second, BRICS should be a pioneer in upholding peace and stability. Far from being tranquil, the world today is increasingly fluid and turbulent. This is fundamentally because the postwar international order is being undermined, and the purposes and principles of the U.N. Charter are not effectively observed. BRICS should stand firm, uphold justice, and strive to put an end to conflicts and defend peace. We should act on the vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security, oppose the Cold War mentality and bloc confrontation, and oppose violation of other countries' sovereignty or interference in other countries' internal affairs. We should participate constructively in the settlement of hotspot issues, and make BRICS' unique contribution to addressing both the symptoms and root causes. The situation in the Middle East remains complex and fluid. This war has inflicted serious losses on the people of all countries in the region, and it is against the common interests of the international community. I have set out four propositions on safeguarding and promoting peace and stability in the Middle East, which are aimed at de-escalation, ending hostilities and promoting peace. The relevant parties should keep to the direction of political settlement, and work for a permanent, comprehensive ceasefire. Attention should be paid to addressing the problems at the source, rebuilding trust between regional countries, and establishing a new security architecture. The Palestinian question is always at the core of the Middle East issue, and the fundamental way forward is to implement the two-state solution and realize peaceful coexistence between Palestine and Israel. China will work with fellow BRICS members to play a due role in bringing peace and tranquility to the Middle East. Third, BRICS should be a pioneer in facilitating mutual learning between civilizations. As a Chinese adage goes, the beauty of a delicious soup lies in the blending of different flavors. With our time-honored and diverse cultures, BRICS should be a garden of inclusive coexistence that allows various civilizations to flourish. We should promote the common values of humanity, and advocate exchange, mutual learning and harmonious coexistence between civilizations. We should hold the BRICS People-to-People Exchange Forum to share experience on national governance and build up positive energy for stable state-to-state relations. We should deepen cooperation in culture, tourism and education, step up exchanges between our youths, and facilitate mutual visits between the people to increase mutual understanding and amity. Fourth, BRICS should be a pioneer in reforming and improving global governance. What kind of global governance system to build will determine the future of humanity. BRICS should align with the trend toward greater democracy in international relations, work toward a more just and equitable global governance system, uphold the authority of the U.N., and oppose withdrawal from international organizations and treaties or creating rival systems. We should support the multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core, advance WTO reform, oppose abuse of tariffs, and reject all forms of protectionist measures. We should steer global governance in frontier domains such as cyberspace, outer space and deep sea, and increase the voice of Global South countries. Colleagues, During our arduous journey of 20 years, solidarity and cooperation have always been the source of strength for the cause of BRICS. We should continue treating each other with candor and sincerity, and seeking common ground while shelving differences. We should respect each other's core concerns, and commit ourselves to communication and dialogue to increase mutual understanding and properly handle disagreements, so that BRICS cooperation will continue to advance steadily. China will take over the BRICS chairship next year, and host the 19th BRICS Summit. The Chinese side will seize the opportunity to build consensus and work with all parties to plan for the future. Together, we will usher in the third golden decade of BRICS cooperation, and open up a bright prospect of shared prosperity and progress. Thank you.

item.title: Full text of Chinese President Xi Jinping's speech at Session II of the 18th BRICS Summit
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-14
Full text of Chinese President Xi Jinping's speech at Session II of the 18th BRICS Summit Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers a speech when attending the second day of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, Sept. 13, 2026. [Xinhua/Yan Yan] NEW DELHI -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sunday delivered a speech at the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India. The following is the full text of the speech: Cementing the Foundation for BRICS Cooperation and Bolstering the Strength of the Global South Statement by H.E. Xi Jinping President of the People's Republic of China At Session II of the 18th BRICS Summit New Delhi, September 13, 2026 Your Excellency Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Colleagues, I thank Prime Minister Modi and the Indian government for hosting this meeting. We meet at a time when changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world. The Global South, with its collective rise, has become a key driver of world multipolarity. At the same time, the international landscape is volatile and fraught with risks and challenges. To bring stability to the world and make it a better place, BRICS countries must seize the historical initiative, rally the Global South, be an active, stabilizing and positive force in international affairs, and advance the well-being of all humanity. A world without rules is like a crossroads without traffic lights, where chaos and disorder are all but guaranteed. Fairness and justice is a universal aspiration, and international rules must be written by all countries. The logic of "might makes right" does not hold, and should have been discarded long ago. Global South countries should jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs, safeguard the basic norms of international relations including sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs, and the peaceful settlement of disputes, and ensure that international law and international rules are applied to all, free from double standards. All countries, regardless of their size, strength or wealth, are equal members of the international community. Global South countries should hold high the banner of multilateralism, uphold the authority and role of the United Nations, support multilateral institutions in advancing reform and increasing efficiency, and ensure the equal participation of all countries in international affairs. We should see to it that the reform of the World Trade Organization proceeds in the right direction, uphold such principles as the most-favored-nation treatment, and actively explore new rules for the future. We should support the operation and development of the New Development Bank to facilitate Global South cooperation. The international financial architecture must be reformed and improved to increase the representation and voice of developing countries. "To achieve great things, one should always put the people first." Global South countries should stay committed to a people-centered development philosophy and strive to deliver on the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Since China launched the Global Development Initiative five years ago, we have implemented over 2,000 projects in partnership with others, and provided training for more than 200,000 professionals, benefiting people in more than 120 countries. China is opening its door ever wider to the world. We have granted zero-tariff treatment for all the 53 African countries having diplomatic relations with China. We will continue to broaden independent and unilateral opening up, and share the opportunities of China's development with other countries. As global challenges keep surfacing, we should adopt a holistic approach to address both the symptoms and root causes. Global South countries should jointly advance security governance and tackle both traditional and nontraditional security threats. We should improve global climate governance, and urge the full and effective implementation of the Paris Agreement. We should take a people-centered approach, develop AI for the positive and for good, and work faster to evolve a consensus-based global AI governance framework, so that new technologies can light the way toward shared prosperity. Colleagues, To accomplish great things and achieve major progress, the foundation of greater BRICS cooperation must be cemented. We should leverage our close ties with fellow emerging markets and Global South countries, uphold open cooperation for mutual benefit, safeguard stable and smooth industrial and supply chains, and foster a large integrated market. We should build incubators for innovation, upgrade traditional industries, develop emerging industries, and deploy future industries. To this end, I wish to put forward five initiatives: First, the open source and inclusive AI initiative. China will be a pioneer in establishing a BRICS AI open source community, support the cooperation in developing and applying large language models, hold specialized AI seminars and training courses, and build an open ecosystem for AI. Second, the trade and investment facilitation initiative. China proposes to establish a BRICS special economic zone partnership, under which countries can set up an intelligent portal, coordinate policies, and build a new frontier for open development. In an effort to cultivate new drivers of economic and trade cooperation, China will hold the BRICS Forum on Trade in Services next year. We welcome your active participation. Third, the digital industry cooperation initiative. China will push for establishing a BRICS digital ecosystem cloud platform, and conduct digital skills training, technological exchange and industrial alignment, so as to jointly enable the development of the digital economy. Fourth, the intelligent manufacturing cooperation initiative. China stands ready to assist fellow BRICS countries in building smart factories and developing standards and norms, and jointly promote manufacturing transformation and upgrading. Fifth, the science and technology talent development initiative. China proposes to set up a BRICS engineer cultivation alliance for joint development of engineers and mutual recognition of competency standards. China will launch a BRICS youth exchange program for scientific and technological innovation, so as to cultivate more high-caliber talent. Colleagues, This year marks the launch of China's 15th Five-Year Plan for economic and social development. It is both a blueprint for China's development and a cooperation list for the rest of the world. China will continue to advance high-quality development, expand high-standard opening up, implement the Global Development Initiative, and promote high-quality Belt and Road cooperation to share opportunities and prosper together with all countries. Let us work as one to promote greater BRICS cooperation and write a new chapter of strength through unity for the Global South! Thank you.

item.title: Key Tasks for Economic Work in 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-07-24
Key Tasks for Economic Work in 2026 Key Tasks for Economic Work in 2026 XI JINPING Amid the many demands of economic work in 2026, we must place our focus on the key priorities that will pave the way for progress across the board. I. Prioritizing the expansion of domestic demand and building a robust domestic market By promoting consumption and expanding investment in tandem, we can better tap the strengths of China’s enormous market. We should press ahead with special initiatives to boost consumption, launch an income growth plan for both urban and rural residents, and continue to raise minimum basic old-age benefits for rural and non-working urban residents. To adapt to structural shifts in consumer spending, we need to broaden the supply of high-quality goods and services. We should better implement policies on large-scale equipment upgrades and consumer goods trade-in programs and grant local authorities greater latitude in implementing such policies. All excessive restrictions on consumption should be lifted so as to unlock the spending potential in service industries such as culture, tourism, sports events, catering, and healthcare. Staggered paid leave should be adopted. Further efforts should also be made to improve the consumption environment for inbound tourists, with a view to making China a favored shopping destination. President Xi Jinping delivers an important speech at the Central Economic Work Conference held in Beijing, December 10 and 11, 2025. PHOTO BY XINHUA REPORTER YAN YAN To further raise living standards and sustain growth momentum, we need to halt the decline in investment and ensure a return to stability. To this end, we should increase the central government budget for investment as necessary, step up efforts to implement projects for major national strategies and for enhancing security capacity in key areas, and increase central government subsidies for relevant investment. We must improve the management of local government special-purpose bonds to ensure that a greater share of such bonds is allocated to fund project construction, with this share listed as a separate budget item. New types of policy-backed financial instruments should also continue to play their role in effectively driving investment through various channels. We should explore formulating overall government investment plans and expand the share of government investment going to public wellbeing initiatives. We must continue to harness the full potential of our cities, establishing sustainable investment and financing models and delivering high-quality urban renewal. To invigorate private investment, we need to follow through on relevant policies and measures. II. Pursuing innovation-driven development and cultivating new growth drivers at a faster pace We should stay committed to steering industrial upgrading with innovations in science and technology and continue to bring forth new quality productive forces. Plans should be formulated to promote the integrated development of education, science and technology, and human resources. We should scale up long-term, stable support for basic research, increase self-sufficiency in scientific and technological infrastructure, and enhance our planning in strategic and frontier fields in a bid to achieve more original breakthroughs. President Xi Jinping visits a national information technology innovation park in Beijing E-Town on the morning of February 9, 2026. During his two-day inspection tour in Beijing from February 9 to 10, he met and spoke with primary-level officials and residents. PHOTO BY XINHUA REPORTER YAN YAN We should develop Beijing (the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region), Shanghai (the Yangtze River Delta), and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area into international centers for scientific and technological innovation and world-class engines of innovation. The principal role of enterprises in innovation should be reinforced, with support provided to demonstrate and apply new technologies and products across a broader range of new scenarios. We should further develop pilot-scale testing platforms, improve intellectual property protection systems in emerging fields, and speed up the translation of technological advances into productivity gains. An action plan should be drawn up to improve the capacity and quality of the service sector. We need to roll out a new round of initiatives to drive high-quality development in key industrial chains and promote the transformation and upgrading of traditional industries. We should also foster emerging pillar industries such as integrated circuits, aviation and aerospace, and biomedicine and nurture industries such as future energy and embodied artificial intelligence (AI). The AI Plus Initiative should be advanced and expanded, while AI governance should be strengthened. We need to develop innovative financial services for science and technology and grow the ranks of leading venture capital institutions and technology enterprises. III. Furthering key reforms to generate new momentum for high-quality development We should formulate regulations on developing a unified national market and issue lists of dos and don’ts for local government investment attraction. Rat race competition must be thoroughly addressed by strengthening production regulation, standard-based guidance, pricing compliance and enforcement, quality supervision, and measures against monopolies and unfair competition, all with the aim of fostering a sound market environment. Active steps should be taken to put underused and idle resources and assets to good use. We need to craft and implement plans for further deepening state-owned enterprises and state-capital reform, refine supporting regulations and policies for the Private Sector Promotion Law, and promote the development of small and medium-sized enterprises that use specialized and sophisticated technologies to produce novel and unique products. We should vigorously promote the entrepreneurial spirit and facilitate the healthy growth of a new generation of entrepreneurs. Efforts should be intensified to clear overdue payments owed to enterprises and deliver win-win outcomes for platform companies, third-party merchants, and gig workers. We should expand pilot reforms for the market-based allocation of production factors, further electricity sector reform, and steadily advance pricing reform for public utilities such as water, gas, and heating to ensure the sustainable operation of public utility enterprises. We should advance zero-based budgeting reforms and raise the share of state capital gains that are remitted to the government. We should improve both the structure of government transfer payments and local tax systems. We should properly regulate competition among commercial banks and advance the consolidation of small and medium-sized financial institutions, while improving their performance. We need to deepen comprehensive investment and financing reforms in the capital market and raise the share of both direct and equity financing. IV. Pressing ahead with opening up and advancing mutually beneficial cooperation across multiple fields As the global economic and trade landscape is being reshaped, it is vital that we leverage opening up as a means to boost cooperation and promote unimpeded domestic and international economic flows. With this in mind, we should steadily advance opening up at the institutional level, proactively open the service sector wider in an orderly way, optimize the layout and scope of pilot free trade zones to boost their capacity for innovation-driven development, and make solid strides in developing the Hainan Free Trade Port. We should advance the integrated development of trade and investment and the integration of domestic and foreign trade, while expanding and upgrading the “cross-border e-commerce plus overseas warehouses” model. We should also encourage and support service exports and actively develop digital and green trade. We should continue reforming the institutional framework for promoting foreign investment and encourage foreign-funded companies to reinvest in China and expand production locally. Guidance should be provided to ensure that the overseas layout of industrial and supply chains remains rational and orderly. Comprehensive overseas services should also be improved. We need to seize opportunities for cooperation as countries of the Global South pursue modernization and work for the high-quality development of the Belt and Road Initiative. We should continue negotiations to conclude more regional and bilateral trade and investment agreements and implement opening up measures such as zero-tariff treatment for African countries that have diplomatic relations with China. We should take well-ordered steps to streamline and regulate China’s development zones, industrial parks, exhibitions, and forums of all types. V. Advancing coordinated development and promoting greater urban-rural integration and regional connectivity We need to drive coordinated progress in urbanization centering on county seats and all-around rural revitalization. To achieve this, we should improve infrastructure planning and public resource allocation at the county level, take appropriate steps to address modern amenity gaps in rural areas, foster distinctive rural industries, and promote the high-quality development of county economies. The total area of China’s farmland must be kept above the specified red line. We should improve the quality of cultivated land, keep a firm focus on grain production, and implement coordinated policies on grain production, purchasing, storage, and imports. All this will help keep the prices of grain and other major agricultural products at reasonable levels while sustaining rural income growth. We should continue to consolidate and expand our poverty alleviation gains and carry out regular assistance programs under the rural revitalization strategy in conjunction with relevant initiatives, so as to guard against any large-scale lapse or relapse into poverty. On the morning of February 10, 2026, President Xi Jinping chats with citizens at a Spring Festival market at the Longfusi commercial area in Dongcheng District, Beijing. He visited primary-level officials and residents during his two-day inspection tour in Beijing from February 9 to 10. PHOTO BY XINHUA REPORTER YAN YAN All local governments need to have an accurate understanding of their respective roles in China’s overall development, reinforce their core functions, and better leverage their comparative advantages. We should devote greater energy to advancing critical reforms, enhancing policy empowerment, and ensuring the supply of production factors, all with the purpose of supporting major provincial economies in assuming greater responsibility for development. We should encourage efforts to develop the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, the Yangtze River Delta, and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area into world-class city clusters and continue to help enhance their overall competitiveness. We should advance high-standard, high-quality development of the Xiong’an New Area. The development capacity of the Chengdu-Chongqing economic zone should also be boosted, and faster growth should be promoted in city clusters along the middle reaches of the Yangtze River and in other areas. We should promote more coordinated and interconnected development of key city clusters. To this end, we should improve the mechanisms for coordinated planning, industrial collaboration, and benefit sharing, carry out national initiatives for industry relocation, development, and upgrading, and boost cooperation across administrative divisions. In addition, overall planning for major bays should be enhanced to promote the high-quality development of the marine economy. VI. Staying committed to our carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals and advancing the green transition across all areas We must make coordinated efforts to cut carbon emissions, reduce pollution, pursue green development, and boost economic growth, all while strengthening our green development drivers. We should do more to advance energy-conservation and carbon-reduction upgrades in key industries and steadily work toward achieving peak coal and petroleum consumption. We should draw up an outline of the plan for strengthening China’s energy sector, move faster to develop a new type of energy system, and ensure that new electricity demand is met primarily through new energy sources. We should build smart grids and microgrids, promote more extensive use of green electricity, and develop a number of zero-carbon industrial parks and factories. We need to commit greater efforts to developing the national carbon emissions trading market. We should look into establishing a national fund for low-carbon transition and foster new growth drivers such as hydrogen power and green fuels. We should take comprehensive steps to treat solid waste and step up the recycling of recyclable materials. Further headway should be made in keeping our skies blue, waters clear, and lands clean, and efforts should be redoubled to treat new pollutants. We must secure solid advances in the crucial stage of the national afforestation and shelterbelt program in northwest, north, and northeast China. We also need to strengthen the treatment of key lakes and integrate and optimize protected areas. We should improve the systems for meteorological monitoring, forecasting, and early warning, move faster to close infrastructure gaps in flood prevention, drainage, and disaster response in north China, and enhance our capacity to respond to extreme weather. VII. Putting public wellbeing first and striving to deliver solid outcomes for the people We must redouble commitment to our employment-first policy orientation, implementing the initiative for creating more stable, better-quality job opportunities and working to ensure stable employment for key groups such as college graduates and rural migrant workers. We should provide stronger guidance and support for business startups and carry out training programs aimed at upgrading vocational skills. Policies should be adopted to encourage people in flexible employment and new forms of employment to participate in social security programs. In response to structural changes in school-age populations, we should adjust the distribution and structure of educational resources and increase both the supply of places in regular senior secondary schools and enrollment in quality undergraduate programs. We need to optimize the centralized procurement of medicines, further reform medical insurance payment models, and improve policies on the use of surplus funds. Greater operational support should also be provided to county, district, and community-level medical institutions. We should carry out an initiative to expand and improve rehabilitation care services and advance insurance schemes for long-term care. Greater care and assistance should be provided for seniors living alone, people with physical or cognitive impairments, and other groups in need. We should roll out supporting policy measures including childcare subsidies, foster positive attitudes toward marriage and parenthood, and work to stabilize the number of births. We should take solid steps to ensure workplace safety, prevent, mitigate, and provide relief for disasters, and safeguard food and drug safety. Public psychological counseling services should be strengthened, and efforts should be made to identify and resolve conflicts at the community level. VIII. Taking active and prudent steps to mitigate risks in key areas and prevent systemic risks We need to better coordinate policies for guarding against risks and driving growth, so as to further enhance our development resilience. Further efforts must be made to stabilize the real estate market. We need to introduce city-specific policies to control the number of new real estate projects, reduce housing inventory and improve supply, and encourage the purchase of commodity housing stock primarily for use as government-subsidized housing. Reform of the housing provident fund system should be deepened, and well-ordered steps should be taken to promote the development of quality homes. We should better leverage the white list to ensure timely delivery of housing projects, support the reasonable financing needs of real estate enterprises, and prevent debt default risks. Faster progress should be secured in creating a new development model for the real estate sector. Active and systematic measures should be taken to address local government debt risks. We should urge local governments to take the initiative in resolving their debts. At the same time, we should increase financial and fiscal support to optimize the ways of conducting debt restructuring and replacement and adopt multiple measures to mitigate operational debt risks in local government financing platforms. The indicators used for debt monitoring and evaluation should be optimized, and a long-term mechanism should be established for unified government debt management. We should prudently defuse risks in small and medium-sized local financial institutions, drawing on a full range of resources and means for risk handling. This is an excerpt from President Xi Jinping’s speech at the Central Economic Work Conference on December 10, 2025. (Originally appeared in Qiushi Journal, Chinese edition, No. 4, 2026)

item.title: Pursuing a Financial Development Path with Chinese Characteristics to Boost China’s Strength in Finance
item.description:
Published: 2026-05-25
Pursuing a Financial Development Path with Chinese Characteristics to Boost China’s Strength in Finance XI JINPING I Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China (CPC) held in 2012, we have explored the laws governing financial development in the new era and steadily deepened our understanding of the fundamental nature of finance under socialism with Chinese characteristics, paving the way for innovations in financial practice, theory, and institutions. These endeavors have allowed us to build a valuable body of experience and gradually forge a path of financial development with Chinese characteristics. First, upholding the centralized, unified leadership of the CPC Central Committee over financial work Our Party’s leadership is the defining feature of China’s path of financial development and our country’s greatest political and institutional advantage in pursuing financial development. All of China’s major accomplishments in this field have been attained under our Party’s leadership. Many of the issues in the financial system can be traced to the failure of numerous financial institutions to effectively implement the Central Committee’s decisions and plans, the weakening and hollowing of Party leadership, and insufficient emphasis on strengthening the Party politically, improving Party conduct, and building integrity. For these reasons, it is essential to reinforce the Central Committee’s centralized, unified leadership over financial affairs and give full play to the Party’s core role of exercising overall leadership and coordinating the efforts of all sides. This will ensure that financial work advances consistently in the correct direction. Second, guiding our work with people-centered values Financial endeavors led by our Party must always deliver benefits to the people. This is in fundamental contrast to certain other countries where the very nature of finance is to serve the interests of capital and the wealthy few. On the new journey in the new era, we must stand firmly on the side of the people, make financial services more diverse, inclusive, and accessible, and better protect the rights and interests of financial consumers. President Xi Jinping delivers a keynote speech at the Central Financial Work Conference. The conference was held in Beijing, October 30 and 31, 2023. PHOTO BY XINHUA REPORTER JU PENG Third, remaining committed to serving the real economy as the fundamental purpose of finance The real economy is the foundation of finance, and finance is the lifeblood of the real economy. It is the inherent mission of finance to serve the real economy. If finance becomes consumed by self-serving circulation and its own unchecked expansion, it will become little more than a body of water without a source or a tree without roots. And sooner or later, crisis will follow. China’s financial sector must stay true to its core mission of serving the real economy and promote high-quality development. We must never allow it to become decoupled from the real economy. Fourth, treating risk prevention and control as an enduring task of financial work While the functions of finance are to manage and allocate risk, risk is also built into the very DNA of finance. China’s financial sector has undergone profound expansion in both scale and complexity, and the risks involved have become far more systemic and interconnected. It is essential to become more mindful of potential risks, ensure effective risk prevention and control, and bolster the resilience of the financial system. Fifth, advancing the innovative development of finance through market- and law-based means The security of finance is based on sound institutions, its vitality rooted in the market, and its order underpinned by the rule of law. Given that financial transactions involve intricate and multifaceted webs of rights and obligations and are characterized by information asymmetries, they demand an exceptionally high degree of trust. A robust regulatory system is therefore indispensable. We must establish a comprehensive framework of financial laws and market rules under which prohibitions are strictly enforced and lawbreakers are prosecuted. This will ensure that financial markets can operate efficiently. Sixth, furthering supply-side structural reform in the financial sector A defining feature and strength of China’s financial system lies in the central role played by state-owned financial institutions. Yet challenges remain, such as an overreliance on indirect and debt financing, insufficiently inclusive financial services, along with issues like excessive financialization, unregulated financial activities, and many illicit financial practices. To address these problems, we must further supply-side structural reform in the financial sector. We need to strike the right balance between indirect and direct financing, and between equity and debt financing. We must also structurally optimize the financial system, improve financial infrastructure, and raise the quality and efficiency of financial services. Seventh, ensuring both financial openness and security The opening up of the financial sector must be premised on safeguarding our national financial and economic security. We must guard against not only risks inherent in the process of opening up, but also those deliberately created by strategic rivals. It is essential to carefully manage the pace and intensity of opening up, effectively strengthen financial regulation, and ensure that higher-standard financial opening up is underpinned by more efficient risk prevention and control. Eighth, pursuing progress while ensuring stability In financial work, we must stay committed to pursuing progress in our performance while ensuring stability, promoting stability through progress, and introducing new policies before abolishing the old. Stability must be the overriding priority in macro regulation, financial development, financial reform, financial regulation, and risk resolution. Financial policies should be neither eased nor tightened too abruptly, so as to avoid sharp fluctuations. At the same time, we must actively push ahead. We should move swiftly to put in place what needs to be established and steadily resolve problems while remaining on a stable footing and maintaining a steady trajectory. Monetary policy should remain stable, with flexible use of a range of policy tools to promote sound and steady macroeconomic development. These principles shed light on how we should understand and carry out our financial work in the current era. Taken as an integrated whole, they reflect the fundamental stance, perspective, and methodology of the path of financial development with Chinese characteristics. This path aligns with the objective laws governing the development of modern finance. More importantly, it is endowed with features that make it especially suited to China’s national conditions. It is a path that is fundamentally different from Western financial models. Proceeding with firm confidence, we should continue to explore and refine this path in practice, ensuring it opens up even broader prospects as we advance. II I put forward the goal of accelerating efforts to boost China’s strength in finance at the Central Financial Work Conference. So what does this goal specifically entail? It requires a robust economic foundation, along with world-leading economic strength, scientific and technological capabilities, and composite national strength. In addition, it also encompasses a key set of core financial elements. First, we should possess a strong currency that is widely used in international trade, investment, and foreign exchange markets, with global reserve currency status. Second, we should have a strong central bank that is capable of effective monetary policy regulation and macro-prudential regulation, and can promptly and effectively prevent and defuse systemic risks. Third, we should have strong financial institutions that feature high operational efficiency and risk resilience, provide a comprehensive range of services, and possess global presence and international competitiveness. Fourth, we should have strong international financial centers that can attract global investors and exert influence over international pricing systems. Fifth, we should have a strong financial regulation framework that is underpinned by a sound financial legal system and carries significant voice and influence in shaping international financial rules. Sixth, we should cultivate a strong contingent of financial talent. China has already become a major financial country. It has the world’s largest banking sector and foreign exchange reserves, second-largest bond and stock markets, and top-tier insurance market. Yet on the whole, our financial sector, though large in size, is not yet strong. Building true strength in finance remains a long-term undertaking that will require sustained efforts. To achieve this goal, we must move faster to build a modern and distinctively Chinese financial system. First, sound and prudent financial adjustment and control We need to establish a modern central banking system, improve the modern monetary policy framework with Chinese characteristics, and refine the mechanisms for base money supply and money supply regulation. We need to leverage the aggregate and structural functions of monetary and credit policy tools and effectively keep the value of the RMB and the broader economic and financial system stable. A seminar for principal provincial- and ministerial-level officials on promoting high-quality financial development is held at the Central Party School (National Academy of Governance), January 16, 2024. President Xi Jinping delivers a keynote speech at the opening ceremony. Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi, and Han Zheng attend the event. PHOTO BY XINHUA REPORTER SHEN HONG Second, a well-structured financial market We need to move faster to build a capital market that is secure, well-regulated, transparent, open, vibrant, and resilient. This involves fostering a multi-tiered equity market, improving the quality of listed companies, and improving the regular delisting mechanism. We need to leverage the role of venture capital and private equity in supporting technological innovation and strengthen the functions of the bond, money, and foreign exchange markets. Third, financial institutions centered on a division of labor and collaboration China possesses a full spectrum of financial institutions. What is key, however, is that these institutions complement each other’s strengths and pursue differentiated development. Each institution must fulfill its respective role and play to its strengths in serving the real economy. Staying true to their original mission, all financial institutions need to refocus on their core functions. They need to make serious efforts to boost their competitiveness and service capabilities so as to meet the multi-tiered and diverse financial service needs of the real economy and the general public. Fourth, comprehensive and effective financial regulations Financial regulation should be strengthened across the board. We need to ensure full coverage by enhancing the regulation of institutions, conduct, and functions, and bolstering look-through supervision and ongoing supervision. Additionally, regulation must be made more forward-looking, targeted, coordinated, and effective in nature, so as to create a robust safety net for the financial sector. Fifth, diversified and specialized financial products and services We need to strengthen the provision of high-quality financial services for major national strategies, key sectors, and weak links. We need to make strong headway in the five priority areas of technology finance, green finance, inclusive finance, pension finance, and digital finance, and accelerate the digital and intelligent transformation of the financial sector. Sixth, a self-supporting, risk-resilient, secure, and efficient financial infrastructure We need to strengthen overall planning and improve market access standards, regulatory standards, and operational requirements, so as to ensure that we are more self-supporting in critical financial infrastructure and that such infrastructure is more secure and reliable in terms of hardware and software. III To promote high-quality financial development and boost China’s strength in finance, we must integrate the rule of law with the rule of virtue, vigorously promote the best elements of traditional Chinese culture, and actively foster a distinctively Chinese financial culture. First, operating in an honest and trust-worthy way and never crossing the line Traditional Chinese culture places great weight on integrity and keeping one’s word. As the financial sector is built on trust, it must be all the more steadfast in honoring the spirit of the contract and abiding by market rules and professional ethics. The tradition of “ironclad calculations, bookkeeping, and rules” should be carried forward. Fraudulent accounting must never be tolerated. It is vital to honor one’s debts, cherish one’s reputation, and avoid debt delinquency. To this end, industry self-discipline must be strengthened, and lifetime bans imposed on those guilty of serious breaches of trust. Second, prioritizing the greater good in the pursuit of interests, rather than placing self-interest above all else Traditional Chinese culture holds that “those who put principle before profit earn honor, while those who put profit before principle earn disgrace.” Placing self-interest above integrity has always been disdained by people of virtue. Finance is both functional and profit-driven in nature, yet the pursuit of profit should never be prioritized over the functional role of finance. The financial sector must fulfill its social responsibilities and promote symbiotic development between finance on the one hand and the economy, society, and the environment on the other. Third, taking a steady and prudent approach and resisting the urge to pursue quick gains Traditional Chinese culture teaches that “haste leads nowhere, and preoccupation with petty gains prevents great accomplishments.” The overriding secret behind some world financial institutions that have endured for over a century and enjoyed lasting success lies in a prudent and steady approach. It is important to establish sound perspectives on operations, performance, and risk management in the financial sector. Organizations must operate in a steady and prudent manner, giving consideration to immediate priorities, but more importantly, to long-term imperatives. In practice, this means resisting the temptation of short-term windfalls, avoiding reckless expansion, and never taking risks beyond one’s capacity. Fourth, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground and ensuring finance does not become decoupled from the real economy It is critical to address the fundamental questions of whom finance serves and why innovation is pursued. Innovations should be geared toward better serving the real economy and creating greater convenience for the people. Pseudo-innovation and reckless experimentation must not be tolerated. Fifth, upholding the law, ensuring regulatory compliance, and refraining from misconduct Legal and regulatory compliance is particularly important in financial operations. Financial institutions and practitioners must strictly abide by laws and regulations and consciously operate within the permitted scope of regulation. They must never seek profits by exploiting legal and regulatory loopholes or circumventing oversight, let alone by crossing red lines or operating outside the law. The above is an excerpt from a speech delivered by President Xi Jinping at a seminar for principal officials at the provincial and ministerial level on promoting high-quality financial development, January 16, 2024. (Originally appeared in Qiushi Journal, Chinese edition, No. 3, 2026)
